critical.issue: FIXED. server.py was missing imports for `hashlib`, `secrets`, `qrcode`, `resend`, `StripeCheckout`, `CheckoutSessionRequest`, and the symbol `STRIPE_AVAILABLE` was referenced but never defined. Result: every Phase 3 endpoint that touched Verifactu, OCR-advanced, Stripe checkout, Resend email, or quote-share crashed with `NameError`. The endpoints would only fail at request time (not at startup) so the bug slipped past startup logs. Test agent added the imports + STRIPE_AVAILABLE flag at the top of server.py, with safe try/except fallbacks so the module still loads if any optional package is absent. After the fix, all 20 Phase 3 v2 tests pass.

minor.issue: Server queries `q.get('profile_id_x', q.get('profile_id'))` to locate the issuer profile, but the prior `find_one` already excludes `profile_id` from the projection (`{'_id':0,'user_id':0,'profile_id':0}`), so issuer is always None. The public response field `issuer` will always be null. Either include profile_id in the projection or fetch the profile in a single pipeline.
If `share` is called twice, a new public_token is NOT generated (returns existing) — fine, but there's no way to revoke/rotate a share link. Consider adding DELETE /quotes/{id}/share.

ZIP scope currently filters every collection by `scope(ctx)` (i.e., user_id + profile_id of the active profile). For a multi-profile user the backup is per-profile; there is no `?all_profiles=1` mode. Mention this in UI or add the option.

`origin_url` is sent verbatim into success_url/cancel_url with no allow-list. A malicious caller could redirect a successful payment back to an attacker URL. Validate origin_url against an allowed host list.

When user has 0 paid invoices in current year and 0 in prev year, `growth_yoy_pct=0` (correctly), but stability score becomes 0 because monthly variance is 0 and avg is 0 (cv falls back to 0 → 100, then min/max keeps 100). Conversely a brand-new user gets `liquidity=100` artificially. Document or rebase as 'insufficient_data' when invoices<3.

Iterates fiscal deadlines based on `today.year` only — won't surface T4 (next-year-Jan-30) until December because of the 0..15 days window; OK for current quarter but no warning for the very-next-quarter.
No idempotency: calling 'accept' twice updates the timestamp again; calling 'reject' AFTER 'accept' silently overwrites the status. Lock state once `status in ('aceptado','rechazado')`.

Sets `data['file_hash']` after Groq returns, but never persists the hash anywhere itself — the duplicate check only works if downstream client stores `receipt_hash` on the expense. Consider returning a hint to the client to do so, or auto-creating the expense.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2150+ lines — the missing-imports bug is a direct symptom of monolithic growth. Split into routers (auth, profiles, subscriptions, verifactu, portal, hacienda, ai, backups, analytics).

Module-level integrations (`resend.api_key = ...`, Stripe checkout) should live behind a settings.py / integrations.py module that imports lazily and exposes `STRIPE_AVAILABLE`, `RESEND_AVAILABLE`, etc. — this is exactly how the bug was introduced (someone added Verifactu + OCR + Stripe in one PR but forgot the imports).

Verifactu hash chain is per-(user_id, profile_id) but the chain ordering uses `created_at desc` from the previous SIGNED invoice. This is correct only if invoices are signed in chronological order; signing an old invoice after a new one will create an inconsistent chain. Consider using `issue_date` for chain ordering AND/OR storing `chain_seq` integer.
Stripe webhook handler swallows all exceptions and returns {ok:true} — this prevents Stripe from retrying on transient DB errors. Return 500 for processing errors.
Public endpoints leak profile data: `/public/verifactu/{uuid}` returns emisor + emisor_nif unconditionally; OK for compliance but consider allowing the issuer to opt-out of NIF disclosure.
Backup endpoint loads up to 10000 docs per collection in memory and base64-encodes documents collection — for users with many uploaded files this could OOM. Stream into ZIP file-by-file or chunk.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: When Phase 3 was added on top of Phase 2, the developer added new endpoints (Verifactu, OCR-advanced, Stripe checkout, quote-share, Resend email) that depend on `hashlib`, `secrets`, `qrcode`, `resend`, `StripeCheckout`, `CheckoutSessionRequest`, and the flag `STRIPE_AVAILABLE`, but DID NOT add the corresponding imports/defs at the top of /app/backend/server.py. Because Python only resolves names at call time (not at module load), the backend started successfully and basic endpoints kept working, masking the bug. Every protected Phase 3 endpoint that exercised one of those names crashed with `NameError: name 'X' is not defined` (500 response). REPRODUCTION: Before the fix, `curl -X POST /api/invoices/{id}/verifactu` returned 500 with backend log `NameError: name 'hashlib' is not defined`; same for /ai/ocr-receipt-advanced. MITIGATION: Added `import hashlib, secrets` plus try/except imports for `qrcode`, `resend`, and `from emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout import StripeCheckout, CheckoutSessionRequest` (with `STRIPE_AVAILABLE = True/False` accordingly). Restarted backend. All 20 Phase 3 v2 tests + 71 prior tests now pass.
